title: Scan editor, extension, and integration surfaces for missed shared-module adoption
scope: H31 editor/integration scan across extensions/**, sublime/**, src/integrations/**, editor tooling under tools/tui/**, and packaging entrypoints tools/package-vscode.js and tools/package-sublime.js.

summary.overallAssessment: These surfaces already share some of the right low-level primitives, but there are still three clear adoption seams: the VS Code extension retains a vendored Windows wrapper implementation that should track the shared wrapper policy more deliberately, several integration CLI entrypoints repeat direct-execution and repo-root/index bootstrap patterns that can converge on existing shared helpers, and TUI packaging/supervisor surfaces still have partially separate runtime/config/artifact conventions that should reuse shared low-level helpers while keeping UI/session behavior local.

highestPriorityHotspots.whyItMatters: The extension launches the CLI on Windows and already carries a mirrored wrapper implementation. Drift here reintroduces the same wrapper bugs that have already been fixed centrally.

highestPriorityHotspots.category: integration CLI bootstrap and direct execution
highestPriorityHotspots.whyItMatters: Integration entrypoints build user-facing payloads and should not each re-derive repo-root/index-dir/bootstrap rules or direct-entry guards.
The TUI is an editor-adjacent surface with its own packaging and supervisor layer. Drift here affects release verification, artifact collection, and runtime behavior.

hotspotMatrix.name: VS Code extension carries a vendored Windows wrapper implementation
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Treat the extension wrapper implementation as a vendored mirror of the shared Windows wrapper policy and keep it synchronized with the shared version rather than evolving it independently.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: The extension package needs local files, but it should not own an independent wrapper policy. The shared module is already the canonical bug-fix point.
testsToRequire: VS Code windows-cmd parity tests against the shared implementation
extension packaging tests that ensure the vendored wrapper files remain present and aligned

hotspotMatrix.name: Integration CLI entrypoints repeat repo-root/index bootstrap and direct-execution logic
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Use the shared direct-execution helper for entrypoint gating, keep shared repo-relative changed-input parsing in cli-helpers.js, and only hoist additional bootstrap pieces when the semantic fit is exact.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: These CLIs are structurally similar, but not identical. Reusing the exact low-level helpers removes drift without flattening each tool into one generic wrapper.
testsToRequire: CLI parity tests for graph/context-pack/impact/API-contract surfaces
symlink or launcher-entry regressions if direct-execution logic is migrated

hotspotMatrix.name: Integration surfaces still depend on tool-side dict-utils for repo-root/index bootstrap
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Do not deepen this dependency. Record it as a migration target for a later proper src-shared repo/workspace/cache-root helper family rather than broadening tools/shared imports further.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: The cross-layer seam is already known to be imperfect. Increasing adoption now would make later extraction harder.
testsToRequire: No direct migration under #420 unless a replacement shared surface exists
Follow-on extraction should be covered by integration/core parity tests

hotspotMatrix.name: TUI runtime/config/artifact surfaces partially duplicate low-level helper behavior
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Share low-level runtime/config/wrapper/serialization behavior where it cleanly matches existing modules, but keep session protocol, UI lifecycle, and capture semantics local to the TUI surface.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: The TUI has real product-specific behavior. The right cleanup is at the helper boundary, not by forcing the supervisor or protocol model into generic shared modules.
testsToRequire: TUI wrapper behavior, startup handshake, and artifact collection regressions whenever low-level helpers change
release verify-surface tests where TUI packaging/runtime behavior is affected

hotspotMatrix.name: Sublime plugin surfaces are largely API-client and UI specific
sharedModules: tools/api contracts and response payload conventions
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Treat this as a mostly no-adopt zone from the JavaScript shared-module perspective. Keep Sublime-specific Python UI/task behavior local and only align payload conventions with the API/editor contract surfaces.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: Cross-language plugin code should not be forced into JS shared-module patterns. The real shared contract here is payload shape and command semantics, not implementation reuse.

mappings.problemSurface: Windows wrapper policy in editor tooling
Integration CLI direct execution and repo-relative helper reuse

mappings.noAdoptRationale: Do not expand the tools/shared dependency from integration/core surfaces; handle this through later H32 extraction work.

localExceptions.reasonToRemainMostlyLocal: Editor session UX, command registration, and process orchestration are VS Code specific even when wrapper/runtime helpers should align.
Supervisor state machine, session protocol, and artifact semantics are TUI-product specific.

localExceptions.reasonToRemainLocal: Python plugin implementation should stay local; the real shared contract is payload and command semantics, not code reuse.

localExceptions.reasonToRemainMostlyLocal: Provider/session logic already uses many shared low-level primitives and remains domain specific beyond that point.

localExceptions.reasonToRemainSelective: Core orchestration should keep its product-specific stage model while adopting low-level shared helpers where exact fit exists.

recommendedFollowUps.why: The integration-to-tools/shared dict-utils seam should be replaced by a real shared repo/workspace/cache-root/generation family.
If VS Code/TUI wrapper and runtime cleanup still feels fragmented after H31, formalize the broader subprocess/toolchain helper family.
If integration payload builders for search/risk/context-pack still repeat too much after selective adoption, create the dedicated shared helper family there.
Editor/API/CLI parity helpers and fixture-driven harnesses may belong in the shared test-harness issue once the adoption patterns are clearer.
